speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how many companies have since closed down due to pressures from the COVID-19 pandemic; and (b) what are the current and future efforts to support local firms for post-crisis growth to maintain our status as an international business hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In the last two years, the Government has committed substantial resources to help our businesses weather the immediate impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are also helping our businesses prepare for post-COVID-19 recovery and continuing to enhance Singapore's position as a business hub in several ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, we are gradually and carefully reopening our borders to more countries through arrangements such as the Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our ports are kept operating throughout the pandemic to ensure supply chain resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will continue to enhance both our air and sea connectivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government is similarly extending Singapore's digital connectivity by establishing a network of Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) with like-minded partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are also investing in digital infrastructure and capability building for our businesses and workers to access such opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In addition, we are partnering with industry stakeholders in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: An example is the SGTraDex, which is a common data infrastructure that enables our businesses to transit into the digital domain.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It also builds a stronger and more robust supply chain ecosystem for international trade flows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As part of the Singapore Green Plan 2030 announced earlier this year, we will help our enterprises and workforce harness sustainability as a competitive advantage, and develop innovative solutions for the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These include, amongst others, carbon trading and related services, low-carbon solutions, green finance, and green infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Thirdly, we are helping businesses transform for the future economy, sector by sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Future Economy Council chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Heng is currently refreshing the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) to meet the accelerated changes brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For each of the 23 ITMs, we are working with our tripartite partners, including the private sector to update our sectoral strategies to seize new opportunities, as well as to improve productivity and wages of our workers through digitalisation, innovation, internationalisation, upskilling and job redesign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These are the fundamentals which will underpin our competitiveness and ensure that Singapore remains as a global-Asia node for technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are confident that through close partnership with Singaporeans as well as the business community, we will be able to emerge stronger together.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Minister of State give us a sense of the growth outlook across the sectors, especially the sectors where business formations are taking place?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We have heard about digitalisation and the formation of DEAs and how it would help Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Could you elaborate a little bit more about MTI's plan to grow the capabilities and the potential of enterprises in sustainability or even in the green economy?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First, he asked about the growth outlook by sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The recovery in tourism related, aviation related or consumer-facing sector is projected to be gradual, in comparison.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He asked about the business formation numbers in sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Business formations continue to flourish, in spite of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on, I cited the numbers, the formation number and the number of firms that closed.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: More new businesses have started compared to the number of businesses closed.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the same period, he asked about sectors, the sectors with the largest number of new businesses formed included professional services, wholesale trade and retail.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It was launched by Minister Gan Kim Yong about a month back on the 1 October.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Enterprise Sustainability Programme does not just support our SMEs at the enterprise level.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is very important for us to also take a sectoral view and an ecosystem-wide approach.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, MTI and ESG will certainly work very closely with the trade associations and chambers (TACs), industry partners, to develop a vibrant sustainability ecosystem to support our SMEs in their sustainability efforts, from capability development to product development.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the same time, taking an ecosystem-wide approach to leverage key enablers like financing, certification, training and other sustainability services.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I want to use the opportunity to assure the Member Dr Wan Rizal and the House that the Government is fully committed to support the growth and the future of our SMEs in the post-COVID-19 recovery.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, we will continue to support our SMEs to adapt and develop their businesses to seize new opportunities, whether in internationalisation, digitalisation or sustainability, and other areas.
